A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable main text, equations, figures, references and appendices. Earlier appendix analyses can be matched reliably despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v5 reports original synthetic Gaussian experiments and analyses of translation, ImageNet-1k and Flickr30k representations, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v6 retains those empirical analyses and adds original cross-layer comparisons, multilingual Qwen3-8B results, language-resource correlations and a CLIP context-length control.

M1.justification: The Information Imbalance procedure and token aggregation methods remain unchanged. Section 2.3 rewrites the nearest-neighbor sum equivalently; the additional model and layer comparisons extend evaluation rather than modify the method.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds WMT17 alongside Opus Books and expands coverage from six to twelve English–other-language pairs. Newly evaluated languages include Latvian, Czech, Russian, Chinese, Turkish and Finnish, substantially broadening language-family and script coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 1 adds RSA, implemented as Spearman rank correlation, to the comparison with CKA and Neighborhood Overlap. The original comparators remain; Norelli et al.'s method is discussed but not evaluated as a new baseline.

E3.justification: Figure 1c's reported Gaussian dimensionality changes from 10,000 to 100,000. New protocols compare fixed first, central and last layers against all other layers, evaluate Qwen3-8B using 1,000 samples per language filtered to 30–80 tokens, and restrict a CLIP comparison to captions fitting its 77-token context.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds extensive analyses of layer-dependent asymmetries within and across models and languages. Appendix F investigates language resources and linguistic family, while Section 3.2.2 adds a caption-length control for CLIP. Earlier shuffling, aggregation and vision-model sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix F introduces Pearson correlations, permutation-based significance testing and results with and without the Chinese outlier. Existing subsampling and jackknife uncertainty reporting remains unchanged; an increase in repetition counts is not documented.

E6.justification: v6 adds RSA, cross-layer and multilingual results, plus the matched-caption comparison reporting approximately 0.18 for CLIP versus 0.11 for DeepSeek-V3 to DinoV2. Figure 6 substantially changes the CLIP layer profile. Section 3.2.2 revises textual minima from 0.20 to 0.10 for DeepSeek-V3 to DinoV2 and from 0.30 to 0.25 for CLIP; the unchanged DinoV2 curves identify its revision as a reporting correction. Appendix F's correlation is inconsistent: -0.86 in prose versus -0.82 in Figure 14.

T1.justification: New Appendix A defines copula-rank variables and restricted mutual information, then states an exponential bound relating the latter to Information Imbalance and discusses tightness. This is a limited formal addition based on prior work, with the full derivation deferred to a cited source.

C1.justification: v6 removes the abstract's suggestion that model scale may outweigh explicit multimodal training. The main claims about distributed token semantics, layer-dependent convergence and asymmetric predictability across languages, models and modalities remain.

C2.justification: v6 qualifies the scale-versus-joint-training interpretation using image-gpt-large as a counterexample and removes the heuristic equating II around 0.2 with roughly 25% shared features. It also adds conjectures about late-layer asymmetry and interpretations of language-resource correlations, including qualifications concerning Chinese and linguistic family.

D1.justification: v6 documents the new language experiment's sample counts and token-length filtering, identifies scipy.stats.PermutationMethod, and explicitly states CLIP's 77-token context limit and image-gpt-large's 1.4-billion-parameter size.

R1.justification: v6 adds references to Bojar et al., Nelsen, Norelli et al., Spearman and Umar et al. It also explicitly acknowledges asymmetric comparison in model stitching and relates the multimodal findings to post-hoc alignment of unimodal encoders. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to the abstract, explanatory examples, synthetic-metric discussion and multimodal interpretation, with new appendix sections and updated cross-references. Most existing prose and the main section organization are retained.

P2.justification: New Figures 10–14 substantially expand the visual presentation with cross-layer comparisons, broader multilingual profiles and a resource-correlation scatterplot. Figure 1 adds RSA curves and revised dimensionality labels, and Figure 6 changes the CLIP directional legend. The original Figure 10 is retained as Figure 15.

improvement.justification: Cross-layer analyses and the CLIP context-length control address weaknesses in v5's supporting evidence, while broader language coverage and a more cautious scale interpretation strengthen the paper. These gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies: Appendix F's correlation disagrees with Figure 14, and the retained description of relatively flat CLIP profiles conflicts with the substantially revised Figure 6.
